newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED SET TO END ENGLAND'S 12-YEAR ABSENCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED SET TO END ENGLAND'S 12-YEAR ABSENCE.

text.p: Manchester United look set to eliminate Porto and become the first English team to reach the semifinals of the European Cup for 12 years on Wednesday.
United take a four-goal lead into the second leg of their quarter-final after their 4-0 win over the Portuguese champions at Old Trafford on March 5.
Barring a totally unexpected collapse against a side who have three key players suspended, United should clinch a place in the last four where they can expect to meet Borussia Dortmund of Germany.
The last English team to reach the semifinals of Europe's premier club tournament were Liverpool in the ill-fated spring of 1985.
Liverpool defeated Panathinaikos of Greece 5-0 on aggregate to qualify for the final against Juventus which they lost 1-0.

But the disaster in the Heysel Stadium on the night of the match in which 39 mostly Italian fans lost their lives, led to the five-year-ban on English clubs playing in Europe. Since English clubs returned to the European Cup in 1991, none have made it to the last four.

Borussia, 3-1 up from the first leg, should be able to defend that lead at Auxerre in the second leg in France, even though they will be without the influential Stefan Reuter, sent off in the first leg.
If they do that they will be at home to almost certainly Manchester United in the first leg of the semifinal on April 9, with the second leg at Old Trafford on April 23.
The other two ties are more finely balanced, although holders Juventus should see off outsiders Rosenborg Trondheim in the second leg back in Italy after a 1-1 draw in Norway two weeks ago.

Atletico Madrid, who drew 1-1 with Ajax in Amsterdam in the first leg of their tie, have home advantage for the second leg and could well end the Dutch side's bid for a third successive European Cup final appearance. Ajax are not helped either by having Patrick Kluivert suspended for two bookings in the competition.
The winners of the Juventus-Rosenborg tie play the winners of the Ajax-Atletico tie in the semifinals.
In the UEFA Cup on Tuesday French league leaders Monaco start as strong favourites to finish the job they started against Newcastle two weeks ago by capitalising on their 1-0 first leg away win.

Newcastle will have Colombian striker Faustino Asprilla back following suspension from the first leg but will still be without world record signing Alan Shearer (groin) and his striker partner Les Ferdinand (hamstring).
Schalke, 2-0 up from the first leg, will have to guard against complacency at Valencia, while Brondby are intending to adopt safety-first methods against Tenerife to guard their 1-0 first leg lead.
Inter, looking to win the UEFA Cup for the third time in seven years, are at home to Anderlecht after drawing 1-1 in Belgium in the first leg.

In the Cup Winners' Cup Fiorentina, 2-0 ahead against Benfica, and Barcelona, 3-1 up against AIK Stockholm, already have one foot in the semifinals, while AEK Athens and Liverpool will be hoping to make home advantage tell after away draws in their ties.

AEK drew 0-0 at PSG, while Liverpool came away from Brann Bergen with a 1-1 draw in the first leg, with the English club hopeful of maintaining its interest in the only European competition it has yet to win.
